jobs.title: Director, Sales & Operations Planning
jobs.jd_full:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve.

Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals.

About the Role:

We are seeking a strategic, process-driven Director of Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) with a strong focus on operations planning, resource management, and labor modeling. This role owns the integrated planning function responsible for translating business strategy into executable operational plans that balance capacity and labor against service and cost targets. This is a highly visible leadership role, setting the operations planning strategy and partnering directly with senior leadership across the organization to shape network-wide decisions. Additionally this role will be responsible for evolving the department - partnering with cross functional teams to create newer and more accurate models that leverage industry best practices and expertise.

You Will:

  • Own the Operations Planning Strategy: Set the vision and governance for the S&OP process, chairing the weekly S&OP meeting and driving alignment between demand signals and executable operations plans across the network.

    • Define the KPI framework and accountability structure that governs plan execution across sites and functions.

  • Fulfillment Capacity Strategy: Own medium- to long-range capacity planning across the network, setting the strategy for personnel, equipment, and material capabilities, and making the call on when network routing or footprint changes are needed.

  • Labor & Resource Planning Leadership:

    • Own the translation of volume plans into required hours by role and process path, and the labor models that drive it.

    • Serve as the primary executive partner to HR, Finance, and Operations leadership in aligning staffing strategy with operational demand across the network.

    • Develop and recommend the long-range workforce strategy by anticipating volume trends, seasonal spikes, and the labor impact of strategic initiatives.

    • Provide recommendations on cross-training, temporary staffing, and overtime strategy based on network-wide capacity constraints.

  • Operational Scenario Modeling: Direct scenario planning to simulate the impact of volume changes, labor availability, or supply disruptions, and translate the results into leadership recommendations and contingency plans.

  • Cross-Functional & Executive Alignment: Serve as the primary point of accountability across compounding, dispense and fulfillment, planning, and finance to ensure operational readiness, resolving cross-functional trade-offs and escalations.

  • Process Optimization: Set the roadmap for continuous improvement in planning processes and models, driving initiatives that improve modeling accuracy, increase efficiency or increase visibility.

  • Performance Management & Reporting: Own the dashboard and KPI strategy for plan adherence, resource utilization, labor efficiency, and production performance, and use it to drive decisions at the leadership level.

  • Executive Communication & Influence: Present operational insights and capacity trade-offs to executive leadership as needed, shaping strategic decisions on network investment, staffing, and capacity.

  • Team Leadership & Development: Build, lead, and develop a team of planners and analysts, establishing career paths and elevating planning capability across the organization.

You Have:

  • Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Supply Chain, or related field (MBA or Master's preferred).

  • 12+ years of experience in operations planning, resource management, or labor modeling in a manufacturing, warehouse, or industrial setting.

  • 8+ years of people leadership experience, including managing teams larger than 6.

  • Proven track record setting operations planning strategy at a multi-site or network level.

  • Expertise in workforce planning, labor forecasting, and operational planning, with deep fluency in translating data into executive-level strategy.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with advanced skills using tools such as Excel, Power BI, Tableau, or labor planning software.

  • Excellent executive presence and communication skills, with a demonstrated track record of influencing C-suite/senior leadership decisions.

  • Experience leading the implementation or selection of labor planning tools or workforce management systems at scale.

Our Benefits (there are more but here are some highlights):

  • Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles

  • Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days

  • Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave

  • Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)

  • 401k benefits with employer matching contribution

  • Offsite team retreats

We are committed to building a workforce that reflects diverse perspectives and prioritizes ethics, wellness, and a strong sense of belonging. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you're not sure if your background or experience is a perfect match.

Your privacy is important to us, and any information you share will only be used for the legitimate purpose of considering your request for accommodation. jobs.jd_full:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

THE ROLE

Sr. Manager, Global Procurement (Soft Home - Bedding)

We are seeking an exceptional Sr. Manager, Global Procurement (Soft Home - Bedding) to own and drive cost structures and savings. This role is critical to our goal of delivering the highest quality products, at radically low prices, done right. Reporting to the Head of Procurement, the ideal candidate will leverage their deep expertise in commodity costing, clean sheet, manufacturing excellence & efficiency (consumption,C&M excellence), harvest timing, raw material availability to craft a competitive costing environment where major T1 and T2 suppliers are being challenged to provide transparent and competitive pricing to achieve a win win supply chain for both Quince and our partners.

Success in this role means achieving product cost at or near should-costing, securing supply continuity, and contributing to product excellence by aligning material procurement processes with the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our business, contribute to company growth, and shape the future of our global sourcing strategy.

Responsibilities

  • Procurement Category Strategy: Define and execute the commercial roadmap and vendor distribution strategy for assigned categories to improve margins as Quince scales. Establish short- and long-term procurement targets aligned to business growth.
    • Consistently deliver exceptional product cost without sacrificing product quality or ESG considerations, including Procurement.
    • Partner with the technology team to embed procurement capabilities and playbook into the Vendor Portal and Product Catalog tools.
    • Identify and deliver 700 bps product cost reductions over the next 12 months.
  • RFP Ownership & Execution: Structure and run competitive, end-to-end bidding processes to secure optimal cost and commercial terms with manufacturing partners. Own the full lifecycle from vendor identification through award.
    • Deliver immediate, best-in-class product cost savings through rigorous negotiation, while simultaneously institutionalizing repeatable negotiation frameworks to build long-term category maturity and sustainable competitive advantage.
    • Build AI agent to help us run RFP systematically in 2026 with the capability to build scenario analyses.
  • Clean Sheet & Buy Plan Approvals: Create and utilize component-level “clean sheets” to drive pricing transparency; review, approve, and solution to optimum cost for all buy events within your categories.
    • Current mature / scale categories: Ensure scale / cleansheet costing with Finished GoodsManufacturers Negotiate upstream of Finished Goods to secure best pricing and availability of (inputs (e.g. fabrics, yarns, fibers, commodities, trims) New categories / new products
    • Lead Buy Plan margin review to govern company margin targetPartner with material sourcing team to ensure transparent, competitive pricing from all key material suppliers (we own material, we own costing)
    • Negotiate reasonable launch costing and set schedule (monthly, quarterly, at trigger points) to renegotiate for scale pricing as the business grows
    • Support merchandising team by providing scale costing targets (i.e. what cost is achievable at scale)
  • Upstream Sourcing: Partner directly with the Material Manager, Sourcing Teams and Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors to align on, and implement, material benefits into finished goods costing.
    • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate upstream material availability into product design and development cycles, ensuring early-stage cost optimization and seamless material-to-finished-good transitions.
  • Value Creation: Identify and execute on opportunities to reshape the supply chain and extract new financial value beyond traditional sourcing boundaries, including verticalization and volume consolidation plays.
    • e.g. How do we become a market maker for Cashmere, Silk, etc? Could we sell cashmere and silk to other retailers? How can we partner with other mills or manufacturers to build a verticalized supply chain for critical materials, like linen, from French/Belgian farms and scutchers to linen mills? How do we buy/sell commodities to manage price fluctuations (e.g. gold pricing, Cashmere pricing)?

Qualifications

Required:

  • 12-15 years of experience in global procurement, sourcing, or supply chain management in a consumer goods or retail environment
  • Proven track record running competitive RFP processes with international manufacturing partners
  • Hands-on experience building and leveraging clean sheets for cost negotiation
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision making
  • Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, materials, and production teams

All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Pay Range

$164,000—$240,000 USD

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form. We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. Initial communication is primarily via official Quince email addresses and LinkedIn; beware of deviations. Personal data and sensitive information will not be solicited during the application phase. Interviews are conducted via phone, in person, or through the approved platforms Google Meets or Zoom—never via messaging apps or other calling services. Offers are merit-based, communicated verbally, and followed up in writing. If personal information is requested to initiate the hiring process, rest assured it will be through secure and protected means.

jobs.title: Product at Nash
jobs.jd_full:
Product at Nash

The Role

Join Nash, an autonomic logistics platform helping enterprises plan, execute, and manage deliveries across diverse fleets, partners, and networks. As a Product Manager, you’ll be at the heart of shaping innovative logistics solutions powered by advanced AI models and integrations. You’ll drive the product vision, collaborating closely with engineering, design, solutions, and go-to-market teams to solve real-world operational challenges for large enterprises.

Our platform operates in highly complex environments, handling orders, inventory, dispatch decisions, delivery updates, and exception management across customer fleets and third-party systems. As a Product Manager, you will translate these workflow challenges into actionable product development, ensuring our solutions deliver measurable value for enterprise customers.

What You’ll Own

  • Define and execute product strategy for core logistics solutions, aligning with business objectives and customer needs.

  • Collaborate with engineering, design, and solutions teams to design, build, and launch features that integrate seamlessly with enterprise OMS, WMS, TMS, and POS systems.

  • Lead product discovery, gathering insights from customers, internal teams, and market research to identify new opportunities and refine existing features.

  • Own the product lifecycle from concept through launch, including scoping, prioritization, requirements definition, and hands-on validation of technical solutions.

  • Work directly with customers and solutions engineers to develop use cases, validate requirements, and ensure each release delivers real workflow improvements.

  • Build and refine product documentation, enablement materials, and value narratives to support sales, customer success, and go-to-market initiatives.

  • Drive analytics and reporting to measure success, understand customer adoption, and identify areas for continuous improvement.

  • Stay hands-on with the latest AI advancements, rapidly testing new models, agent capabilities, and feature prototypes with real-world customer use cases.

  • Serve as a key product evangelist, representing Nash’s vision with customers, partners, and at industry events.

What We’re Looking For

  • 6+ years of product management experience, ideally in SaaS, logistics, supply chain, or enterprise software.

  • Strong technical acumen with hands-on experience in system integrations, APIs, and complex enterprise environments.

  • Proactive discovery and analytical skills—you ask the right questions, explore unarticulated pain points, and transform ambiguous needs into clear requirements.

  • Exposure to AI tools and models, with an understanding of how cutting-edge tech can drive value in operational workflows.

  • Experience working cross-functionally to lead collaborative product development with engineering, design, and technical sales or solutions teams.

  • Ability to draft clear requirements, user stories, and comprehensive use cases based on structured discovery and customer feedback.

  • Excellent communication skills; comfortable presenting to both technical and executive audiences.

  • Ownership mindset—you thrive in fast-paced environments with evolving requirements and can drive initiatives from 0 to 1.

Even better if you have:

  • Previous experience in logistics, delivery, or supply chain technology.

  • Experience shipping AI-native or agent-driven product features.

  • Hands-on data analysis or financial modeling skills to quantify product impact.

  • Flexible PTO and remote-first culture.

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance for US employees

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Caylent is an AI-first cloud services company that helps organizations turn ambitious ideas into meaningful business impact. As an AWS Premier Tier Services Partner and a charter member of Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network, we combine deep expertise in AWS, artificial intelligence, and Anthropic’s Claude platform to help customers modernize their technology, build intelligent products, and move AI from experimentation into production.

Our capabilities span generative and agentic AI, cloud migration and modernization, cloud-native application development, data and analytics, DevOps, managed services, security and compliance, and customer experience transformation. At Caylent, our people always come first.

We are a fully remote global company with employees in Canada, the United States and Latin America. We celebrate the culture of each of our team members and foster a community of technological curiosity. Come talk to us to learn more about what it means to be a Caylien!

About This Role

Caylent's Anthropic Consulting and Engineering (ACE) practice is a dedicated AI services team built in partnership with Anthropic. We are Anthropic's first pure-play delivery partner.

The Agentic SDLC Product Manager owns the Product workstream inside client engagements. On Transformation Blueprint programs, you lead the Product workstream alongside engineering and organizational workstream leads: running current-state assessments with client product teams, designing the future-state PDLC, and coaching product managers through the shift from spec authors to strategic orchestrators of AI-assisted development. On 3-2-1 Build and Enable engagements, you shape the prototype: leading the scoping session, defining the Sprint Charter with the client, and driving the spec generation that feeds Sprint 1 delivery.

You are embedded in client product and engineering organizations from kickoff through handoff. Your clients are product managers and engineering leads who need to redesign how products get built, not just which tools their teams adopt.

What You'll Do

Client Delivery

  • On enterprise transformation programs, lead the product workstream end-to-end: assess how client product teams operate today, design the future-state PDLC, and coach PMs through the shift from spec authors to strategic orchestrators of AI-assisted development
  • On prototype and build-enable engagements, anchor the product side: run discovery with client stakeholders, shape the delivery backlog into a signed Sprint Charter, and write the specs that drive prototype and MVP development
  • Design PM training curricula and lead enablement sessions throughout engagements, using real delivery work as session material
  • Surface expansion opportunities during delivery: by the close of each engagement, you have a clear view of what the client's product org needs next

Agentic IP and Tooling

  • Help define and refine the product-facing agents Caylent deploys across engagements: idea consolidation, spec generation, PM workflow automation, and the product side of advanced agent prioritization
  • Provide field feedback that sharpens agent design, prompt configuration, and the scoping frameworks that determine where agentic tooling fits in client environments
  • Co-own the product spec artifacts that define how Caylent's IP gets built and evolved across the practice

Internal Contribution

  • Turn PDLC patterns from the field into improvements to product workstream methodology, scoping frameworks, and future-state design templates
  • Support pre-sales conversations where product definition, sprint structure, or PDLC maturity assessment is part of the qualification

What We're Looking For

Required

  • 7+ years of product management experience, including meaningful time in a client-facing, embedded, or consulting role
  • Experience working directly with product teams on how they work: their discovery processes, PDLC design, and spec practices
  • Experience or demonstrated capability in the use of Agentic AI to facilitate product management activities
  • Strong facilitation: you run working sessions with product and engineering stakeholders, extract useful signal from ambiguous input, and drive toward a signed-off decision
  • Able to write clean, executable specs, both for your own engagement deliverables and as a model for clients you're coaching
  • Technical fluency to scope prototypes with engineers: you can discuss architectural feasibility, participate in spec-to-build handoffs, and hold your own in an architecture lock session

Preferred

  • Background in professional services, management consulting, or an embedded advisory role
  • Experience redesigning how a product function works inside another organization, not just producing recommendations
  • Familiarity with AI-native product workflows: spec-driven development, LLM-assisted requirements generation, or agentic product tooling
  • Experience with PE portfolio company environments or enterprise engineering organizations navigating modernization
  • Hands-on familiarity with Claude Code or equivalent AI-assisted development tooling

Who Thrives Here

  • Operates inside the client's product function. You're in the roadmap sessions, the scoping workshops, and the spec reviews. Clients let you in because you understand their problems.
  • Makes client PMs better. Your measure of success is whether client product teams can run AI-native workflows after you leave.
  • Owns the diagnosis and the design. You run the assessment, draw the conclusions, and write the future-state design.
  • Can build a sprint with engineers. On prototype engagements, you're defining the Sprint Charter and writing the specs. You can hold a technical conversation about feasibility and push back when scope doesn't fit the architecture.
  • Feeds the methodology. Every engagement teaches you how product organizations respond to AI-native practices. You turn that into the next version of the workstream approach.

This is a poor fit if you're most comfortable in a single-product company where your users are internal and your roadmap is yours to own long-term. Engagements close. You hand off and move to the next client. The quality of what you leave behind is the measure.

Why This Team

  • The Product workstream is one of the most differentiated parts of the Transformation offering and currently the one with the most room to develop. You shape it from the first engagement
  • Each engagement feeds directly back into the workstream materials: field observations change how the offering runs
  • Your clients are PE portcos, enterprise engineering orgs, and Anthropic-referred customers at the frontier of AI adoption
  • AI-native by default: you build with and through Claude, coaching clients on practices you use yourself
  • Outcomes, not hours: advancement tied to workstream delivery quality, methodology contribution, and account expansion

Benefits

  • 100% remote work
  • Equitable Life - Hybrid Plan
  • 100% Premium Coverage for the employee and dependents
  • Competitive phantom equity
  • Long-Term Disability
  • 4% Pension match (employer contribution)
  • Unlimited Vacations
  • Sick Leave
